description: Auto-derive the model repo id from the docker-compose YAML content so the deployer downloads weights to the exact directory the compose file references, fixing the bug where a custom compose that names a model the deployer has never seen (with modelName left empty/wrong) downloads to the wrong path and the container never becomes healthy. Implement a pure-Python, PyYAML-free extraction helper and wire it into BOTH the deployer (primary bug fix: decide the model download path) and the api upload path (persist the derived modelName so the UI/list reflect reality). Frontend modelName stays optional and backward compatible.
steps: Write a pure-Python helper `extract_model_from_compose(compose_content: str) -> str | None` that scans the raw compose TEXT (no yaml import, mirroring the existing api/handler.py::_fallback_has_services_mapping no-PyYAML approach). It must find every occurrence of the path prefix `/opt/dlami/nvme/models/<slug>` regardless of surrounding syntax, so it covers all real writings: SGLang `--model-path /opt/dlami/nvme/models/<slug>`, vLLM `--model /opt/dlami/nvme/models/<slug>`, and shell `MODEL=/opt/dlami/nvme/models/<slug>`. Use a regex like `/opt/dlami/nvme/models/([^\s'"\\]+)` to capture the slug and stop at whitespace/quotes. Strip any trailing path segment after the slug if present (the slug is the first path component after models/). Convert slug->HF repo id by replacing ONLY the FIRST `__` with `/` (org/name; the name may itself contain `__`). Return None when no such path exists (e.g. slime-style compose with no model path) so callers fall back.

Conflict/consistency policy (implement and document in a docstring): collect all distinct slugs found. If zero -> return None. If exactly one distinct slug -> return its repo id. If multiple DIFFERENT slugs -> take the first one encountered and log a warning (logger.warning) noting the others were ignored; do not raise. Multiple occurrences of the SAME slug is the normal case (e.g. docker-compose-pd-2p2d.yaml repeats the path 4x) and must resolve cleanly to one value.

Because api/ and deployer/ are separate Lambda packages with no shared import path, place this helper in BOTH: add it to platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py and to platform/lambda/api/handler.py. Keep the two copies identical in behavior. (Do NOT create a cross-package shared module or a symlink; the packaging step does not support it.) The function must not import boto3 or yaml so it is trivially unit-testable.

Deployer fix in platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py: change the model-name resolution used by _get_compose_commands so the effective priority is: (1) value parsed from the actual compose content via extract_model_from_compose, (2) plan record modelName (the current `model_name` argument), (3) DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME. Concretely: inside _get_compose_commands (or just before it in _handle_deploy), load the compose text (it already calls _load_compose_content(compose_file) inside _get_compose_commands - reuse that same loaded content) and if extract_model_from_compose returns a value, use it for BOTH model_local_path and the HuggingFace snapshot_download model id, overriding the passed model_name. When parsing yields None, keep the existing behavior (model_name arg, then DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME). If the parsed value differs from a non-empty passed model_name, log a warning that the compose-derived model takes precedence. Ensure _load_compose_content is only called once per deploy (avoid a double S3 fetch): refactor so the content is loaded once and both the extraction and the heredoc use the same string.

Built-in plan backward compatibility: the 7 built-in plans (in the hardcoded plan_compose_map / PLAN_MODEL_MAP) currently resolve model_name from PLAN_MODEL_MAP. After this change their compose files all contain `/opt/dlami/nvme/models/deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4-Flash` or `...__DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, which parse back to exactly deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 respectively - identical to the current PLAN_MODEL_MAP values. Confirm this equivalence in a test so the built-in behavior provably does not change.

API upload fix in platform/lambda/api/handler.py::create_deployment_plan: after compose validation, call extract_model_from_compose(compose_content). If it returns a value, use it as the stored modelName. Only when it returns None, fall back to the current logic: (body.get('modelName') or DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL).strip() or DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL. Keep the request field optional (do not add a required field). The stored plan item's modelName is what the frontend list/回显 reads, so this keeps UI consistent with what will actually be deployed.

Add pytest tests in a new directory platform/lambda/tests/. Create platform/lambda/tests/test_extract_model_from_compose.py. Import the helper directly from the module under test (add the package dir to sys.path in the test, e.g. via a conftest.py that inserts platform/lambda/deployer and platform/lambda/api on sys.path, or import by file path). Cover: (a) SGLang --model-path form -> deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash; (b) vLLM --model form with slug nvidia__DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark -> nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark; (c) shell MODEL= form -> nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark; (d) compose with NO model path -> None (fallback case); (e) same slug appearing multiple times -> single consistent repo id (use the real docker-compose-pd-2p2d.yaml content or a 4x-repeat fixture); (f) slug->repo id inversion correctness including a slug whose name part itself contains an underscore stays intact (only first __ becomes /); (g) multiple DIFFERENT slugs -> returns the first and does not raise. Assert the deployer copy and the api copy produce identical results for the same inputs (import both and compare) so the duplicated logic cannot drift silently.

Add platform/lambda/tests/test_upload_modelname.py (or extend the above) verifying create_deployment_plan-level logic only if it can be done without AWS: prefer a focused unit test of the extraction-vs-fallback decision. If create_deployment_plan cannot be exercised without boto3/S3, at minimum unit-test the pure helper and document that the api wiring is covered by reading the code path. Do NOT introduce moto/boto mocking unless trivial.

Add pytest to platform/lambda/requirements.txt ONLY if a dev/test extras convention exists; otherwise leave requirements.txt as boto3-only (it documents RUNTIME deps) and install pytest ad hoc for the test run. Prefer NOT modifying requirements.txt since it explicitly documents runtime-only deps.
acceptance_criteria: extract_model_from_compose exists in BOTH platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py and platform/lambda/api/handler.py with identical behavior and no yaml/boto3 import dependency.
For SGLang --model-path, vLLM --model, and shell MODEL= writings, the helper returns the correct HF repo id (first __ -> /).
For a compose file with no /opt/dlami/nvme/models/ path, the helper returns None and callers fall back to the prior modelName resolution.
Deployer resolves the download path from the compose-derived model when available, else plan record modelName, else DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME; the compose content is loaded once (no double S3 fetch).
create_deployment_plan stores the compose-derived modelName when present, else falls back to body.modelName/DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL; the request modelName field remains optional.
Built-in plans' compose files parse back to exactly the existing PLAN_MODEL_MAP values (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash and -0731), proving no behavior change for the 7 built-ins.
`python3.12 -m pytest platform/lambda/tests/ -v` passes with all new tests green.
verification: Run `python3.12 -m py_compile platform/lambda/api/handler.py platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py` and confirm exit 0.
Run `python3.12 -m pip install -q pytest` then `python3.12 -m pytest platform/lambda/tests/ -v` and confirm all tests pass.
Grep-confirm both handlers define extract_model_from_compose and that _get_compose_commands / create_deployment_plan call it.
findings:
Implemented FEAT-001. Files changed: platform/lambda/api/handler.py, platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py, .gitignore (added __pycache__/ *.pyc .pytest_cache/ so test-run artifacts stay out of the tree). New: platform/lambda/tests/conftest.py, platform/lambda/tests/test_extract_model_from_compose.py, platform/lambda/tests/test_upload_modelname.py.

Helper (identical behavior in BOTH packages): `def extract_model_from_compose(compose_content: str)` returning `str | None`. api copy at platform/lambda/api/handler.py line 525 (just above _fallback_has_services_mapping); deployer copy at platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py line 321 (just above _get_compose_commands). Pure text/regex scan `r"/opt/dlami/nvme/models/([^\s'\"\\/]+)"`, no yaml/boto3 import. Added `import re` to deployer/handler.py (api already imported re). Slug->repo id replaces only the FIRST '__' with '/' via `first_slug.replace('__','/',1)`. Distinct-slug collection preserves first-seen order; multiple DIFFERENT slugs -> first + logger.warning, no raise; same slug repeated -> one value; none -> None.

Deployer wiring: _get_compose_commands now loads compose content ONCE (_load_compose_content) then derives the model. Priority = compose-derived > passed model_name (plan record modelName) > DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME. If derived differs from a non-empty passed model_name, logs a warning and compose wins; model_local_path and the HF snapshot_download id both use the resolved model. No double S3 fetch.

API wiring: create_deployment_plan calls extract_model_from_compose(compose_content) after validation; stores derived modelName when present, else falls back to `(body.get('modelName') or DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL).strip() or DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL`. Request modelName stays optional. DEFAULT_PLAN_MODEL / models.py default unchanged ('deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash').

Backward compat: test proves all 7 built-in compose files parse back to exactly the current PLAN_MODEL_MAP values (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash and -0731). Verified compose files: 5 use --model-path with deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4-Flash(-0731); pd-2p2d.yaml and pd-v4flash-b300.yaml repeat the same path 4x -> resolve to one value.

Tests: conftest loads each handler under a unique module name via importlib (module names collide otherwise, both are 'handler') with the package dir on sys.path. Installed pytest+boto3 for python3.12 ad hoc (`python3.12 -m pip install -q pytest boto3`); did NOT modify requirements.txt (runtime-only, boto3). Tests assert deployer and api copies return identical results across inputs.

Verification results:
1) `python3.12 -m py_compile platform/lambda/api/handler.py platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py` -> exit 0 (COMPILE OK).
2) `python3.12 -m pytest platform/lambda/tests/ -v` -> 44 passed in 0.07s.

TEST-QUALITY FOLLOW-UP: The deployer precedence tests in test_upload_modelname.py previously used a private replica `_deployer_effective_model(...)` that re-implemented the priority logic, so they would still pass even if the real wiring in `_get_compose_commands` were reverted. Replaced that replica and its 4 tests with 3 tests that exercise the REAL `deployer_handler._get_compose_commands('some-plan', 'user-x.yaml', model_name=...)` by monkeypatching the module-level `deployer_handler._load_compose_content` (its only S3 touch) to return a chosen compose string, then asserting on the joined command list's generated `snapshot_download('<model>'` id and `local_dir='/opt/dlami/nvme/models/<slug>'` path. New real-function cases: (1) test_deployer_compose_wins_over_passed_model_name — compose pins nvidia__DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark with a wrong model_name='deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash' passed -> generated commands download 'nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark' into .../nvidia__DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark (the exact bug scenario, compose wins); (2) test_deployer_uses_passed_model_name_when_no_compose_path — slime-style compose (no model path) + model_name='custom/Model-Y' -> downloads 'custom/Model-Y' into .../custom__Model-Y; (3) test_deployer_uses_default_when_no_compose_path_and_no_model_name — no path + model_name='' -> falls back to DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash' into .../deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The api-side `_resolve_upload_model_name` replica was kept (create_deployment_plan needs boto3/S3/DynamoDB; not worth moto) with a docstring note explaining why. handler.py was NOT modified. Re-verified: `python3.12 -m pytest platform/lambda/tests/ -v` -> 43 passed in 0.04s; `python3.12 -m py_compile platform/lambda/deployer/handler.py` -> exit 0.
